extra.message: The 'user_pic' view reads the 'p' query parameter (filename) and joins it directly into a filesystem path via os.path.join(base_path, filename), then opens and returns the file contents. extra.message: The 'missing_access_control' view exposes the admin page based solely on the 'action' query parameter (?action=admin) with no authentication or authorization check. Any unauthenticated user can access privileged/admin functionality.
The 'csrf_image' view is decorated with @csrf_exempt, disabling Django's CSRF protection for this endpoint and allowing cross-site request forgery.

The CsrfViewMiddleware is commented out in MIDDLEWARE_CLASSES, disabling CSRF protection site-wide. All state-changing POST endpoints (e.g. the user profile update in dor_user_profile) are vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery.

The Django SECRET_KEY is hardcoded in source. A known SECRET_KEY lets attackers forge session cookies, CSRF tokens, password-reset tokens, and signed data, compromising the integrity of the application.

DEBUG = True is set. In production this exposes detailed stack traces, settings, source code snippets, and SQL queries to users on any unhandled exception (e.g. via the /misconfiguration/boom endpoint), leaking sensitive information including the SECRET_KEY and environment details.

The 'boom' view deliberately raises an unhandled exception. Combined with DEBUG = True, this returns a full Django debug error page exposing source code, stack frames, settings, and environment variables to the user, resulting in sensitive information disclosure.
